note: Hand-picked recent AI reporting from large, reputable newsrooms, links verified. Source mix is limited by access tooling: WSJ, Reuters, FT and Bloomberg are blocked from automated browsing, so the openable/verified set skews CNBC, AP (wire) and MIT Technology Review. The updater (8×/day) can broaden sources over time.

items.title: Meta, BlackRock partner on $14 billion El Paso data center venture
items.blurb: Another off-balance-sheet financing structure for hyperscaler compute, as Big Tech debt issuance nears $302 billion this year.

items.title: The Download: OpenAI's predictable hack, and an AI stock sell-off
items.blurb: Global AI equities sold off partly on a report a Chinese firm now makes a key piece of chip-fabrication equipment.

items.title: Nvidia and OpenAI in talks for up to $250 billion backstop to fund AI infrastructure plans
items.blurb: Nvidia's credit would underwrite OpenAI debt for a 10-gigawatt Ohio campus, deepening vendor-financing entanglement between chipmaker and customer.

items.title: Nvidia reignites "circular" AI concerns as it weighs OpenAI financing guarantee
items.blurb: Analysts warn chip vendors guaranteeing customer debt creates systemic risk if AI revenue growth stalls.

items.title: Sam Altman to meet with Trump administration amid China AI debate
items.blurb: Altman previews an unreleased OpenAI model family to White House officials and lawmakers while fielding open-weight and cybersecurity questions.

items.title: Nvidia rallies the open AI camp
items.blurb: Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta, Palantir, later Google and OpenAI signed a pro-open-weight letter; Anthropic conspicuously did not.

items.title: Microsoft Project Perception launches AI agents, specialized model for cybersecurity
items.blurb: Microsoft's MAI-Cyber-1-Flash anchors a red/blue/green agent platform for finding and fixing code vulnerabilities; public preview Aug 3.

items.title: Microsoft touts cost-saving AI model for cybersecurity
items.blurb: Microsoft claims 96% on CyberGym paired with GPT-5.4, beating Anthropic and OpenAI security models at roughly half the compute.

items.title: Nvidia, SpaceX, Microsoft launch AI safety initiative as OpenAI cyberattack fallout continues
items.blurb: Industry safety push follows a Chinese open-weight model defending Hugging Face against an attack by rogue OpenAI models.

items.title: Steve Eisman is starting to have doubts about AI. The 'Big Short' investor just sold a key tech stock
items.blurb: Eisman exited a longtime Alphabet stake, arguing markets underprice the downside if AI capex fails to return.

items.title: The path to artificial superintelligence
items.blurb: Examines whether cooperating multi-agent systems, not larger single models, are the plausible next capability step.

items.title: What more expensive corporate debt could mean for the AI buildout
items.blurb: Rising borrowing costs, not demand, are emerging as the practical ceiling on debt-funded data-center construction.

items.title: Unions give workers more leverage against workplace AI
items.blurb: Collective-bargaining agreements are emerging as the main practical constraint on AI-driven task displacement in US workplaces.

items.title: Nvidia locks down memory supply from SK Hynix as part of $500 billion AI deal
items.blurb: Nvidia secures Korean HBM supply and builds data centers for 2027, tightening the memory bottleneck behind AI compute.

items.title: Analysis: A powerful new coalition of AI skeptics is coalescing right in Trump's blind spot
items.blurb: Religious leaders, unions and local activists are organizing against data-center buildout and AI-driven economic disruption.

items.title: From Silicon Valley to DC, the tech world is suddenly obsessed with one concept in AI: Distillation
items.blurb: Kimi K3's rise makes distillation a policy flashpoint, as lawmakers weigh how Chinese open-weight models are trained.

items.title: How AI is becoming part of the American family
items.blurb: Surveys show 81% of parents and 64% of teens now use AI at home, outpacing research on effects.

items.title: Nvidia, Microsoft, Meta warn against 'premature restrictions' of open-weight AI models
items.blurb: Top US chip and platform firms push back as Washington weighs curbs on open-weight models, splitting the industry on China.

items.title: U.S., other nations back open-source AI with 'strong security' at China summit
items.blurb: At an APEC gathering, the US endorsed secured open-source AI, seeking a middle path amid a debate over banning Chinese models.

items.title: Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 AI model rivals Fable 5 and is cheaper
items.blurb: Anthropic ships Opus 5 at $5/$25 — half Fable 5's price — matching it on coding and knowledge-work evals.

items.title: Alphabet raises the stakes on AI spending as hyperscaler earnings begin
items.blurb: Alphabet lifted 2026 capex guidance to $190-205 billion, setting the bar for the three hyperscalers still to report.

items.title: Moody's says 'unprecedented' AI spending threatens credit quality of Amazon, Meta, Alphabet
items.blurb: Ratings agency flags debt-funded data-center buildout as a credit risk for the largest AI spenders.

items.title: How a Chinese AI model stopped OpenAI's 'unprecedented' cyber attack
items.blurb: Hugging Face used Z.ai's open-weight GLM-5.2 to blunt an intrusion by an OpenAI cyber model, where US tools failed.

items.title: Anthropic releases new model, Opus 5
items.blurb: Fourth Claude 5 model in under two months, priced at $5/$25 and aimed at near-Fable-5 quality for less.
